ticket: DOD-1d (plans/tickets_phase8_review.md ticket 8.4), the fourth of the five M2-T10 definition-of-done subtickets. 'Decision-log entries (open-Q #4 + coarse-ledger).' Two entries are in scope: (a) the coarse-ledger property, which ALREADY has a durable decision (LG-1) and is only cross-referenced here, not duplicated; and (b) the open-Q #4 resolution, which had no dedicated decision-log entry and is authored here.
open_q4_statement: Open-Q #4 (raised in plans/milestones/tickets_milestone2.md, deferred from the non-destructive tickets 3/6 to ticket 10): does the graph BECOME the authoritative Tier-3 source — the graph->docs compiler overwrites the ticket-14 hand-lift in place — or does it remain a PARALLEL / diff-only surface that never mutates docs/? Until this resolution, --from-graph was held strictly non-destructive (compile-and-diff) so the question stayed open.
decision: PARALLEL + EXPLICIT PROMOTE. The resolution is a third option that subsumes both poles rather than choosing one. (1) PARALLEL: `python -m runner --from-graph <config>` (runner/graph_compiler.py) stays fully non-destructive — it writes only to docs/tier4_orchestration_state/graph_compile/staging/docs/**, emits diff_report.json (Tier-3, vs the hand-lift oracle) and part_b_report.json (Tier-5), and NEVER writes the canonical docs/ paths. (2) EXPLICIT PROMOTE: a separate, deliberate, human-invoked step — `python tools/promote_graph_staging.py --config <config> --apply` — performs the opt-in cutover staging -> docs/. So the graph CAN become the authoritative Tier-3/Tier-5 source (answering the 'becomes authoritative' pole) but ONLY through an explicit, fail-closed promotion (honouring the 'parallel/diff' pole's safety); the compiler itself never auto-overwrites. This is the resolution already stamped into the run's promote_record.json (`open_q4_resolution: 'parallel + explicit promote (M2-T10)'`) and the part_b_report.json non_destructive note; this entry ratifies and records it per §9.4.

why_not_either_pole.not_pure_auto_overwrite: Letting the compiler write docs/ directly would make a single --from-graph invocation silently mutate the constitutional Tier-3/Tier-5 source that the runner reads and every downstream deliverable traces to (§11.4) — an irreversible-in-one-step, silent-bypass-adjacent hazard (§13.7 in spirit) — and would couple a pure, replayable compile to a destructive side effect, weakening the determinism guarantee DOD-1c relies on.
why_not_either_pole.not_pure_parallel_diff_only: Never promoting would strand the graph as a permanently advisory surface: the milestone-2 thesis (vault -> --from-graph compile -> promote -> runner -> gates) could never actually drive a run from graph-sourced docs, defeating the graph-as-source aim (D15 / §2 agnostic engine). The gated run msca-pf-graph-01 required real graph-sourced docs/ to exist.
why_not_either_pole.why_hybrid_wins: The hybrid keeps the compile pure and byte-replayable (the 'parallel' half, proven deterministic by DOD-1c) AND lets the graph become authoritative on explicit, reversible human action (the 'promote' half). Purity and authority are separated across two commands instead of fused into one destructive compile.

mechanism_and_guards.non_destructive_staging: runner/graph_compiler.py stages to docs/tier4_orchestration_state/graph_compile/staging/docs/** and reports: diff_report.json (record_type tier3_graph_compile_diff; converged=true, residual_total=0 against the ticket-14 hand-lift on the authored vault) and part_b_report.json (record_type part_b_graph_compile; section_count=3; its own non_destructive field states the cutover is deferred to the promote). docs/ is untouched by the compile.
mechanism_and_guards.explicit_promote: tools/promote_graph_staging.py::promote() is the explicit half. Dry-run by DEFAULT (prints what would change); --apply is REQUIRED to write. A human runs it; the graph never runs it for you.
mechanism_and_guards.fail_closed_project_id_guard: promote() refuses (PromoteError) unless the staging's project_id (from part_b_report/diff_report) equals the project_id of the graph.config.yaml passed in — so a stale toy/second-instance staging (e.g. the BorrowBrella agnosticism instance) can never clobber the active docs. Missing staging tree or missing reports also fail closed.
mechanism_and_guards.reversible_provenance: On --apply, every overwritten canonical file is first copied to docs/tier4_orchestration_state/graph_compile/pre_promote_backup/**, and promote_record.json logs {record_type, project_id, apply, promoted_files, changed_files, source_reports, promoted_at, open_q4_resolution, note}. Also fully reversible via git (docs/** is tracked). The hand-lift remains the fallback.
mechanism_and_guards.deterministic_claude_free: The promote is a project-id-guarded byte copy with no domain reasoning — a §17.5.3-class deterministic, Claude-free composition step: same staging => same promotion. Pinned by the new regression seam (idempotent second apply reports zero changes).

grounding_run: The run this resolution closes is msca-pf-graph-01 — the graph-authored Part B (ticket-8 vault) passed the entire Phase-8 evaluator gate chain (gate_10a/10b/10c/10d/11). The on-disk promote_record.json records project_id 'msca-pf-reference' (the config/instance identity — the guard field, DISTINCT from the run-scoped run_id 'msca-pf-graph-01', per the DOD-1c run_id observation), apply=true, and 9 promoted-and-changed files: the 6 Tier-3 architecture_inputs (objectives/outcomes/impacts/workpackage_seed/milestones_seed/risks .json) plus the 3 Tier-5 proposal_sections (excellence/impact/implementation _section.json), promoted_at 2026-07-22.

no_constitutional_amendment_rationale: Whether the graph is promoted by a human command or auto-written by the compiler is an implementation choice about how docs/ (already the §9.1 authoritative layer) is materialised; the constitution mandates neither. No phase meaning, tier meaning, gate condition, or authority-hierarchy rule changes. §9.2 is directly served: graph_compile staging is derived runtime state (rebuildable), so a parallel staging tree never competes with docs/ for authority. §13.7 is honoured, not strained: an explicit, fail-closed, backed-up, recorded promote is the ANTITHESIS of a silent bypass — the opposite of the silent phase-reorder / gate-weakening the clause forbids. §17.5.3 is respected: the promote is a sanctioned deterministic Claude-free component. §11.4 / §9.5 hold: Tier-5 stays derivable from higher tiers and reproducible; the promote only writes the derivation onto canonical paths. Recorded here per §9.4 so a future reader does not mistake the parallel-staging + explicit-promote design for an un-recorded constitutional change.
change_surface: tests/runner/test_promote_graph_staging.py (NEW regression seam: pins the four load-bearing behaviours that make this decision true — non-destructive dry-run default, fail-closed project_id/missing-staging guards, reversible backup + open_q4_resolution-stamped promote_record on --apply, and deterministic idempotent promotion — plus a thin consistency check that this entry records the resolution, identifies open-Q #4/DOD-1d, and references-not-duplicates the LG-1 coarse-ledger decision). tools/promote_graph_staging.py previously had ZERO tests; the mechanism the decision ratifies is now pinned.
NO change to runner/ (the promote tool and the non-destructive compiler already landed in the M2-T10 run), the DAG scheduler, gate evaluator, node-state machine, or any tier source.
re_open_trigger: If a future workflow requires a FULLY-AUTOMATED graph->docs cutover with no human promote step (e.g. a CI pipeline that compiles and promotes in one shot), that is a NEW decision that must re-open open-Q #4 and re-argue the silent-overwrite safety the explicit step currently supplies (the project_id guard, the pre_promote_backup, the promote_record, the git-reversibility) — it is not a mere implementation tweak. Absent such a requirement, 'parallel + explicit promote' stands: the compiler stages, a human promotes.
